lessons.title: Capstone Kickoff: The LTV Global Scenario
lessons.chapterTitle: Capstone: LTV Global Data Governance Program

slots.practicalActivity: Write your own half-page program charter for the fictional LTV Global scenario: restate the UK GDPR data-subject-access-request incident as the business problem in your own words, name all five systems (Atlas, Beacon, Comet, Harbor, Summit) and what each is the source of today, and write one sentence predicting what you expect will be the hardest part of unifying 'customer' across Atlas, Beacon, and Comet. You will refer back to this charter for the rest of the capstone.
slots.deliverable: A half-page written LTV Global program charter naming the trigger incident, all five systems, and a predicted hardest challenge.

lessons.title: Reviewing the Data Landscape
lessons.chapterTitle: Capstone: LTV Global Data Governance Program

lessons.title: Identifying Critical Data Elements
lessons.chapterTitle: Capstone: LTV Global Data Governance Program

slots.practicalActivity: Build a data landscape inventory table for LTV Global listing each of the five systems, the data domains it holds, and where 'customer' or another entity is duplicated across systems. Then score at least four candidate critical data elements (for example OrderTotal, Email, SKU, and one you choose) against a criticality rubric (regulatory exposure, business impact, cross-system reuse) and select which ones formally become this capstone's CDEs.
slots.deliverable: A completed data landscape inventory table, plus a scored list of at least four critical data elements with the rubric applied.

lessons.title: Assigning Data Owners and Data Stewards
lessons.chapterTitle: Capstone: LTV Global Data Governance Program

lessons.title: Building the Business Glossary and Data Dictionary
lessons.chapterTitle: Capstone: LTV Global Data Governance Program

slots.practicalActivity: For each CDE from last hour, name a data owner and a data steward and confirm with a quick RACI check that exactly one role ends up Accountable per element. Then write real business glossary entries (term, definition, owner, approval status) and matching data dictionary entries (table, column, data type) for at least four terms, including a reconciled single definition of 'Customer' across Atlas, Beacon, and Comet.
slots.deliverable: A named owner/steward list with a RACI check for each CDE, plus four business glossary entries and matching data dictionary entries.

lessons.title: Classifying Sensitive Data
lessons.chapterTitle: Capstone: LTV Global Data Governance Program

slots.practicalActivity: Classify at least six real fields from LTV Global's systems (including Email, a payment or card-related field, and one you choose) into sensitivity tiers (Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted), writing a one-line justification for each tier and naming which tier would require masking in a non-production environment.
slots.deliverable: A sensitivity classification table for at least six fields, each with a tier, a justification, and a masking decision.

lessons.title: Creating Data Quality Rules and SQL Checks
lessons.chapterTitle: Capstone: LTV Global Data Governance Program

slots.practicalActivity: Write real, runnable T-SQL data quality rules against the Atlas schema pattern from this lesson (OrderTotal must be positive, Email must be well-formed, SKU must be unique, and a referential integrity check between Orders and OrderLines), then combine all four into one UNION ALL failures report with consistent RuleName and RecordKey columns. Add a fifth rule of your own (for example, Payments.CardToken must never be NULL for a completed order) as an additional branch.
slots.deliverable: One complete SQL script implementing at least five labeled data quality rules combined into a single UNION ALL failures report, run against a real or sample SQL Server database.

lessons.title: Documenting Data Lineage
lessons.chapterTitle: Capstone: LTV Global Data Governance Program

slots.practicalActivity: Trace and document the full lineage of one CDE (for example OrderTotal) from its source table in Atlas, through every transformation hop, into the intended governed Summit warehouse, naming at the system or table name at each hop. Then write how you would use that documented lineage to answer 'where did this number actually come from' if an executive dashboard showed a figure that didn't match Finance's own number.
slots.deliverable: A hop-by-hop lineage trace for one CDE from source to warehouse, plus a written root-cause-tracing walkthrough using it.

lessons.title: Identifying Authoritative Data Sources
lessons.chapterTitle: Capstone: LTV Global Data Governance Program

lessons.title: Designing Access and Retention Policies
lessons.chapterTitle: Capstone: LTV Global Data Governance Program

slots.practicalActivity: For each CDE, formally declare which system (Atlas, Beacon, Comet, or Harbor) is the authoritative source of record, resolving at least one case where two systems currently disagree. Then write an access policy (who may view, edit, or export each sensitivity tier from Lesson 6) and a retention policy (how long each CDE's data is kept and what triggers deletion or archival) for LTV Global.
slots.deliverable: A declared authoritative source per CDE resolving at least one conflict, plus a written access policy and retention policy by sensitivity tier.

lessons.title: Developing Governance KPIs and Workflows
lessons.chapterTitle: Capstone: LTV Global Data Governance Program

lessons.title: Creating the Governance Operating Model
lessons.chapterTitle: Capstone: LTV Global Data Governance Program

slots.practicalActivity: Write five governance KPIs for LTV Global (CDE ownership coverage, quality check pass rate, average issue resolution time, access recertification completion, and access request response time) each with a target value, plus an escalation workflow for a KPI that falls below target. Then choose and justify LTV Global's governance operating model (centralized, federated, decentralized, or a federated hybrid), naming who sponsors it, who sets standards, and who holds day-to-day authority.
slots.deliverable: Five written governance KPIs with targets and an escalation workflow, plus a justified operating model naming sponsor, standard-setter, and domain authority.

lessons.title: Developing the AI Governance Strategy
lessons.chapterTitle: Capstone: LTV Global Data Governance Program

slots.practicalActivity: Apply the five-point AI governance checklist (risk tier, data provenance, bias and fairness, model documentation, monitoring plan) to LTV Global's two AI pilots -- the demand-forecasting model and the customer-service generative assistant -- filling out a model card for each. Name specifically which checks the higher-risk pilot fails and what has to happen (a named owner, scrubbed training data, a human-in-the-loop requirement) before it can go to production.
slots.deliverable: Two completed model cards (one per AI pilot) with assigned risk tiers, plus a written punch list of what the higher-risk pilot still needs before launch.

lessons.title: Designing the Governance Architecture
lessons.chapterTitle: Capstone: LTV Global Data Governance Program

slots.practicalActivity: Draw the target-state governance architecture for LTV Global: source systems feeding a raw zone, a conformed zone gated by your Lesson 7 quality checks, a golden zone for the reconciled Customer record, cataloged in a governance layer, and consumed through reporting and the two AI pilots. Justify your specific platform choice (such as a Snowflake-plus-Purview-plus-Power BI stack) against LTV Global's actual constraints -- not a generic recommendation -- and map each zone to an owner from your earlier work.
slots.deliverable: A diagrammed raw/conformed/golden zone architecture with a justified platform choice and a named owner per zone.

lessons.title: Assembling the Deliverables
lessons.chapterTitle: Capstone: LTV Global Data Governance Program

slots.practicalActivity: Assemble every artifact you have built across this chapter -- the landscape inventory, CDE scoring, owner/steward RACI, glossary and dictionary, classification table, SQL failures report, lineage trace, authoritative source declarations, access/retention policy, KPIs and workflow, operating model, AI model cards, and architecture diagram -- into one organized package of files with a short index page naming what each one is.
slots.deliverable: One organized deliverables package (with an index) containing every artifact built across this chapter's earlier lessons.

lessons.title: Writing the Enterprise Data Governance Strategy
lessons.chapterTitle: Capstone: LTV Global Data Governance Program

slots.practicalActivity: Write the single synthesized strategy document for LTV Global covering all six standard sections: Executive Summary, Current State, Target State, Roadmap, Governance Model, and Success Metrics -- pulling directly from your own package rather than from placeholder language, and ending the Success Metrics section on the same DSAR response-time KPI the Executive Summary opened on, now with a stated target.
slots.deliverable: One complete six-section enterprise data governance strategy document, written as a single start-to-finish narrative.

lessons.title: Building the Executive Presentation
lessons.chapterTitle: Capstone: LTV Global Data Governance Program

lessons.title: Final Review and Retrospective
lessons.chapterTitle: Capstone: LTV Global Data Governance Program

slots.practicalActivity: Compress your strategy document into a five-beat executive presentation (the hook, the cost of inaction stated in time and risk terms, what you built, the roadmap, and one specific ask) and deliver it out loud -- recorded, or to a real colleague or mentor -- in under ten minutes. Then write a half-page retrospective on the whole capstone: which deliverable you're proudest of, which decision was hardest to make, and what you would do differently building this program for a real organization.
slots.deliverable: A recorded or witnessed five-beat executive presentation under ten minutes, plus a written half-page capstone retrospective.

lessons.title: Data Governance Career Paths and Roles
lessons.chapterTitle: Career Preparation

lessons.title: Resume Preparation for Governance Roles
lessons.chapterTitle: Career Preparation

slots.practicalActivity: Search for three real, currently posted data governance job titles online and note which one matches your current experience level. Then write a one-page resume draft using the action + artifact + framework pattern (what you did, what you produced, what standard or tool you used) for at least four bullets drawn directly from your own capstone deliverables -- the SQL failures report, the glossary, the lineage trace, and the operating model -- with real numbers from your own work, not invented ones.
slots.deliverable: Notes on three real governance job postings, plus a one-page resume draft with at least four capstone-grounded bullets in the action + artifact + framework pattern.

lessons.title: LinkedIn and Portfolio Development
lessons.chapterTitle: Career Preparation

lessons.title: Governance Portfolio Review
lessons.chapterTitle: Career Preparation

slots.practicalActivity: Draft a real LinkedIn 'About' section naming your governance capstone and its concrete deliverables, and build a simple portfolio page or README (in a document or a real GitHub repo) listing your capstone artifacts with one-line descriptions and, where appropriate, redacted or illustrative excerpts. Then review it against a checklist: does every claim name a real artifact, is anything overstated, and would you be able to discuss each listed item for five minutes if asked.
slots.deliverable: A drafted LinkedIn About section and a portfolio page/README listing capstone artifacts, self-reviewed against an honesty-and-depth checklist.

lessons.title: Explaining Your Capstone in Interviews
lessons.chapterTitle: Career Preparation

lessons.title: The Governance Interview Landscape
lessons.chapterTitle: Career Preparation

slots.practicalActivity: Write and say out loud your own 90-second Situation/Task/Action/Result answer to 'walk me through your capstone,' timing yourself and revising until it fits under two minutes without rushing. Then write one honest answer to 'what would you do differently' naming a real trade-off from your own capstone work, and one note on which interview format (take-home SQL exercise, panel scenario discussion, architecture whiteboard) you'd expect for the specific role you're targeting.
slots.deliverable: A timed, under-two-minute spoken STAR answer about your capstone, plus a written honest 'what I'd do differently' answer and one noted expected interview format.

lessons.title: Scenario-Based Governance Questions
lessons.chapterTitle: Career Preparation

lessons.title: Data Quality and SQL Interview Practice
lessons.chapterTitle: Career Preparation

lessons.title: Metadata and Lineage Interview Questions
lessons.chapterTitle: Career Preparation

slots.practicalActivity: Pick two of the lesson's scenario-based questions (such as two systems disagreeing on 'customer' count, or an executive dashboard showing a wrong number) and write your own answer from scratch before checking it against the lesson's structure: clarify, name the concept, walk through it, state the outcome. Then write real SQL for one data-quality interview question (such as finding duplicate keys with GROUP BY...HAVING) and one written answer to a metadata/lineage interview question, both drawing on your own capstone artifacts as evidence.
slots.deliverable: Two written scenario-question answers using the clarify/name/walk-through/outcome structure, one real SQL interview answer, and one metadata/lineage interview answer.

lessons.title: Security, Privacy and AI Governance Questions
lessons.chapterTitle: Career Preparation

lessons.title: Stakeholder Presentations and Communication
lessons.chapterTitle: Career Preparation

slots.practicalActivity: Write your own answers to one security/privacy interview question and one AI-governance interview question, each grounded in a real artifact from this course (your classification table, or your AI model card and risk tier). Then deliver a three-minute stakeholder presentation out loud -- to a mirror, a recording, or a real listener -- explaining one capstone decision (your operating model choice, or your architecture) to a non-technical business audience in plain language.
slots.deliverable: Two written interview answers (security/privacy and AI governance) grounded in your own artifacts, plus a delivered three-minute plain-language stakeholder presentation.

lessons.title: Governance Certifications Overview
lessons.chapterTitle: Career Preparation

lessons.title: Working With Data Teams as a Governance Analyst
lessons.chapterTitle: Career Preparation

lessons.title: Salary and Offer Basics
lessons.chapterTitle: Career Preparation

slots.practicalActivity: Look up two real governance-relevant certifications from the lesson (such as CDMP or a vendor-specific catalog certification) and write one sentence on which one, if any, fits your target role. Then write a short note on how you would work with a data engineering team as a governance analyst (what you'd ask them for, what you'd hand back), and research real salary ranges for a governance analyst role in your target location, drafting one sentence you would actually say if negotiating an offer.
slots.deliverable: Notes on two real certifications with a fit decision, a written data-team collaboration note, and researched salary ranges with a drafted negotiation sentence.

lessons.title: Your First 90 Days in a Governance Role
lessons.chapterTitle: Career Preparation

lessons.title: The Long Path to Data Governance Architect
lessons.chapterTitle: Career Preparation

lessons.title: Path Complete: Next Steps
lessons.chapterTitle: Career Preparation

slots.practicalActivity: Write your own real 30/60/90-day plan for a first governance role, naming a concrete first deliverable for each window drawn from this course's skills (a data landscape review in the first 30 days, a first quality-rule set by 60, a first KPI report by 90). Then sketch your personal career ladder from this role toward data governance architect, naming which rung you're on today. Finish with a written paragraph answering 'why should someone hire you for a data governance role,' citing at least three specific pieces of real evidence from across the whole path -- not just this capstone.
slots.deliverable: A written 30/60/90-day plan with concrete deliverables, a personal career-ladder sketch, and a final hire-me paragraph citing at least three pieces of evidence from across the full path.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: After finishing this course -- and with it, the entire Data Governance Engineer program -- a student has personally built one complete, end-to-end enterprise data governance program (landscape inventory, critical data elements with named owners, a business glossary, real T-SQL data quality checks, documented lineage, authoritative sources, access and retention policy, governance KPIs and an operating model, an AI governance strategy, and a target-state architecture), synthesized it into an executive strategy document and presentation, and has a tailored resume, portfolio, and practiced interview answers ready to apply for real data governance analyst, engineer, or architect roles.
